meta.title: Suggestions — options to review and choose between
meta.how_to_use: This is a decision board, not a backlog. Each option states what it fixes, the evidence that it is a real problem, the effort, the risk, and what it unlocks — so one person can pick a path without reading the code. Suggested sequence is by the 'order' field; nothing here has been implemented by this session.

status_legend.accepted: Owner has chosen this path (mark it here before work starts)
status_legend.rejected: Owner has declined (leave the row and the reason, so it is not re-proposed)

meta.rule: A suggestion is only accepted with an owner and a 'definition of done'. An accepted suggestion without a definition of done is how a wishlist becomes a backlog.

rows.title: Make one build the product and archive the other five
rows.fixes: Six live builds that disagree with each other (F-09, Q-06)
rows.evidence: Six entry points are published from one origin; two of them report different error statistics for the same 60 games.
rows.risk: Low — nothing is deleted; every old build stays reachable under /archive/.
rows.unlocks: Every other fix lands once, in one place, instead of five times.
rows.definition_of_done: Root landing page names one current build; the other five are reachable under /archive/ with a dated banner saying which build superseded them and when.

rows.title: Put the edition stamp and the capture time on every number, not in the JSON
rows.fixes: Stale injury layer (F-03, F-04), stale prop lines (F-01), unstated star-signal staleness
rows.evidence: The injury page cites the 04:15 AM edition while the official index offers 1:30 PM; three of four prop lines are below the current official average.
rows.risk: Low — additive. A row with no stamp is marked unverified rather than hidden.
rows.unlocks: A reader can tell, without opening anything, whether a line is still live. This is the single highest-value UI change in the project.
rows.definition_of_done: Every table that shows a derived or captured number carries an 'as of' column or a page-level stamp; a build fails if the stamp is older than the latest official edition on the index page.

rows.title: Publish corrected statistics next to every raw one
rows.evidence: BH q = 0.120 across six tested strategies; edge-size gradient r = 0.051 on n = 32.
rows.risk: Low, and it will make the headline worse. That is the point.
rows.unlocks: The project can be defended. A raw p-value with no multiplicity correction is the first thing a statistically literate reader will challenge.
rows.definition_of_done: Each strategy row shows: record, raw p, BH q, and the edge-size gradient. The landing page headline reads from the corrected figure.

rows.title: Fix the rest/back-to-back field and make both builders read one table
rows.fixes: F-12 — 26 of 27 horizon rows carry a negative rest value; two pages disagree
rows.evidence: Read from scripts/originate_horizon.py and confirmed in data/derived/picks_d.json vs site/data/lines.json for the same game.
rows.risk: Low — a pure bug fix with an assertion that makes regression impossible.
rows.unlocks: Rest becomes a usable signal (Q-09), and the game-flow page stops printing 'B2B' for almost every game.
rows.definition_of_done: rest_days >= 0 for every row, asserted in the builder; one shared rest table consumed by both pages; the two pages agree game by game.

rows.title: Auto-ingest the latest injury edition instead of a hand-captured one
rows.evidence: The official index publishes every 15 minutes on a game day; 22 designations changed between 12:00 PM and 1:30 PM on 11/14.
rows.effort: 2-3 days (the refresh workflow already exists and already reaches the official hosts from GitHub's runners)
rows.risk: Medium — a bad parse could move lines. Mitigation: publish the diff, keep the previous edition, and never let a parse failure move a line.
rows.unlocks: Injury-driven rotation minutes and production, which is an explicit requirement of the brief and is currently a lower bound on stale data.
rows.definition_of_done: Every refresh stores the edition stamp, the parsed rows and the diff; the site shows 'changed since last edition'; the build refuses an edition that is not the newest on the index.

rows.title: Pre-register S1 and stop adding strategies until it resolves
rows.evidence: Six strategies have been tested on the same 60 games. Each additional test raises the bar for all of them.
rows.effort: One hour to write, 60 games to resolve
rows.risk: Low. It costs nothing and it is the only path to a defensible claim.
rows.unlocks: Either a funded strategy or an honest 'no'. Both are better than a headline that cannot survive correction.
rows.definition_of_done: A dated file states S1's exact rule, its grading convention and the number of picks required; the site shows progress against it and refuses to add a strategy before that count is reached.

rows.title: Add a 'decision' layer to the landing page
rows.fixes: The navigation problem (R-18): a reader cannot tell what to do with six builds and 978 table rows
rows.evidence: The current landing page leads with status tiles and a category index; there is no 'what changed, what needs your decision' block.
rows.unlocks: The site becomes usable by someone who has ten minutes, not ten hours.
rows.definition_of_done: Landing page opens with: one sentence of state, three things that changed since the last build, and the open decisions with links. Everything else moves below it.

rows.title: Collect official player game logs for the whole window
rows.fixes: Q-08, and the prop variance work
rows.evidence: The repository holds game logs for 3 players. Every prop-combination price depends on correlations that are currently guessed.
rows.unlocks: Measured parlay correlations instead of assumed ones; prop uncertainty bands that are measured rather than modelled.
rows.definition_of_done: Every player who appears in a published prop pick has his official game log in the repository, with per-game source URLs, and the parlay rho table is measured rather than assumed.

rows.title: Decide the odds question in writing
rows.evidence: No price source exists anywhere in the repository, and every gate that would need one is marked blocked.
rows.risk: None. Doing nothing keeps the question open forever, which is the current state.
rows.unlocks: Either a real market test (with a licensed feed) or a permanently honest framing.
rows.definition_of_done: One paragraph on the landing page and in the README stating which of the two paths the project is on, dated.

rows.title: Give every row one source link, or an in-row 'no official source' mark
rows.evidence: 78 of 978 data rows carry no official link; the build audit uses a narrower row definition than the reader does.
rows.unlocks: The brief's own rule becomes true as a reader would test it.
rows.definition_of_done: Independent HTML parse reports 0 unlinked data rows, or every unlinked row carries a visible 'no official source exists' mark and appears on the Flagged page.

rows.title: De-duplicate the coordination board and make claims atomic
rows.evidence: Seven sections appear twice; two section numbers are shared by different sessions.
rows.risk: Low if the pair is confirmed identical before the earlier copy is removed.
rows.definition_of_done: Every section number appears once; each claim is one commit that only appends; the file has a header explaining the numbering rule.

rows.title: Give the leaderboard a reason to exist beyond ranking
rows.evidence: The leaderboard ranks 10 strategies; 4 have no graded plays at all and none is funded.
rows.risk: Medium — reward structures invite people to game the metric. If a reward is offered, the metric has to be pre-registered and the sample-size floor has to be enforced.
rows.definition_of_done: Written rules: entry condition, metric, minimum sample, tie-break, and what the reward is.
